summary: Two trades, a swap that lowers equity risk. Sell all of MCO, the named first sell candidate under L8: its premise is gone, it is 2.4% above its stop, and it sits in a bucket the Market Analyst avoids. Add $15 to WMT, the one Staples name whose event risk is now behind it (beat and raised guidance today). No other buys: SPY is one close from switching the regime filter off, and the Market Analyst says not to add to VOO/VTI, bonds, gold, crypto or international. Held-book review (L7, L9): no stop has tripped. SPY 730.20 is above both the stored 729.79 line and the Market Analyst's 730.02, so VOO and VTI hold. They are about 23.6% of equity on one stop, and if SPY closes below the line I will propose selling both in full at the next run, as the PM pre-committed on 11-17 and 11-18. FAST's thesis condition 'a marginal hold if XLI keeps lagging' is met: Industrials are still on the Market Analyst's avoid list, and XLI was 4.66% below its 200-day as of 11-18. I am still not proposing a sale. FAST is the lowest-vol name on the menu (0.244, beta 0.51), 15.5% above its own stop, and the stored clause makes it marginal, not broken. If MCO goes, it is the next sell candidate. Other qualitative clauses: WMT's guidance clause is not met (guidance raised per today's 8-K 2.02 and headline). Today's note gives no XLP 21d figure, but the Market Analyst still favors Staples and has them above the 200-day. No guidance cut or negative 8-K for CARG, DPZ, IDXX, MSCI, VRSN, EXEL, INCY or SAM. The INCY and VRSN insider sales are sentiment, not clause events. KR's cyber incident is unconfirmed. Every held stock is still on the 11-17 menu. Cash commitment (L4, due today): with both trades, cash ends near 12.9%, about $18 above the 10% buffer. I am holding that on purpose. The regime is one ordinary session from turning off and the Market Analyst asks for small new equity risk, so the reason is specific to today, not L4.

proposals.thesis: L8 follow-through. On 11-18 the PM restated MCO on quality and low beta after the Market Analyst dropped Financials, named it the first sell candidate, and asked the Proposer for a sell proposal or an explicit hold at this run. This is the sell. The Market Analyst's note today favors only Staples and Utilities and lists Industrials (MCO's packet bucket) among sectors to avoid. He also says credit is weakening (HYG 1.07% and LQD 2.01% below their 200-day) and long yields are rising, which weighs on ratings issuance. The Fundamentals Analyst flags MCO as having the lowest gp_sector_pct of any held name (0.825), and says it fails leverage_not_up, the same failure as MSCI, so the financial-data sleeve has rising leverage in both names (L3). After the sale MSCI (beta 0.37, +5.5% on cost, 14.4% above its stop) remains the sleeve's only name. The stop block shows MCO NEAR at 2.4% above $470. No price stop or stored clause has tripped: no guidance cut, still on the menu, and the News Analyst lists only routine items and the 11-13 8-K 8.01 (inferred notes offering). The sale rests on the lost premise, not on a tripped stop. Tax: one short-term lot opened 11-16 at a small loss (about -$1.36), so there is no long-term timing to protect. The proceeds partly fund P2.
proposals.invalidation: MCO closes back above $509.04 (its fill, about 5.8% above the 481.29 mark) within 20 sessions, or beats SPY over the next 20 sessions.

proposals.thesis: Consumer Staples is one of the two sectors the Market Analyst favors today. He asks that new equity risk stay small and stay in defensive sectors above their 200-day lines, and this buy follows that preference rather than reversing it (L4). WMT's Q3 event has now passed. The News Analyst confirms an 8-K 2.02/9.01 filed 11-19 and the headline 'Walmart Raises Fiscal Year Guidance Amid 3Q Earnings Beat'. That makes WMT the one Staples name with its event behind it; KR still reports 12-03. Earnings date (L2): reported 11-19 per the 8-K 2.02. The next date is unverified because the file still shows today, though last year's pattern points to about late February 2027. Fundamentals: F7, gp_sector_pct 0.863, passes the screen, still on the 11-17 menu. WMT has its own close-based stop, so it does not add to the shared VOO/VTI SPY-200-day stop (L9), and its 252-day beta (-0.058) adds almost no market risk. It is not a hedge. Overlap (L3): WMT, KR and SAM are one Staples factor bet. With P1, the Staples bucket rises from about 16.2% to about 18.6% of equity while the Industrials bucket falls from about 8.9% to about 5.1%. Funded from MCO's proceeds, the swap moves about $24 from a 0.54-beta name in an avoided bucket into a near-zero-beta name in a favored one. It lowers equity risk and does not deploy new cash. Risk: after about eleven PT raises the bar was high, and the price reaction is not in the inputs. If WMT opens more than about 5% above the 127.36 mark, the PM should treat this as chasing and cut or drop it. The WMT position would be about 10.4% of equity, under the 15% cap and the $43.34 room.
proposals.invalidation: WMT closes at or below $119.00 (the stored stop for the whole position, about 6.6% under the 127.36 mark and further under any post-print gap up), or XLP's 21-day return falls below +3% while SPY holds, or the Market Analyst drops Consumer Staples from his favored sectors.
